summary: Anyone can promise to give the Beis Hamikdash a person's erech (the set amount the Torah gives for a person). This mishnah teaches who can promise it and for whom.

chunks.en: Everyone can promise an erech, and everyone can be given an erech.
chunks.explain: An erech is a set amount of money, written in the Torah, to give to the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: Everyone takes vows of valuation and is thereby obligated to donate to the Temple treasury the value fixed by the Torah (see Leviticus 27:3–7) for the age and sex of the person valuated. And similarly, everyone is valuated,
chunks.stMore: and therefore one who vowed to donate his fixed value is obligated to pay.

chunks.en: Everyone can vow to give a person's worth, and everyone's worth can be vowed.
chunks.explain: A person's worth is how much money he would be sold for.
chunks.st: Likewise, everyone vows to donate to the Temple treasury the assessment of a person, based on his market value to be sold as a slave, and is thereby obligated to pay; and everyone is the object of a vow
chunks.stMore: if others vowed to donate his assessment.

chunks.en: This includes Kohanim, Levi'im and Yisraelim,
chunks.st: This includes priests, Levites and Israelites,

chunks.en: women and slaves.
chunks.st: women, and Canaanite slaves.

chunks.en: A tumtum and an androginos
chunks.st: A tumtum, whose sexual organs are concealed, and a hermaphrodite [androginos],

words.note: A person whom we cannot tell is a boy or a girl.
A person who seems to be both a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: can vow a worth, can have their worth vowed, and can promise an erech,
chunks.st: vow, and are the object of a vow, and take vows of valuation,

chunks.en: but they cannot be given an erech,
chunks.st: but they are not valuated.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, if one says, with regard to a tumtum: The valuation of so-and-so is incumbent upon me to donate to the Temple treasury, he is not obligated to pay anything,

chunks.en: because only someone who is surely a boy
chunks.st: as only a definite male

chunks.en: or surely a girl is given an erech.
chunks.st: or a definite female are valuated.

chunks.en: A deaf-mute, a shoteh and a child
chunks.st: A deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor

words.note: Someone who cannot hear or speak.
Someone whose mind is not well.

chunks.en: can have their worth vowed and can be given an erech,
chunks.st: are the object of a vow and are valuated,

chunks.en: but they cannot vow a worth or promise an erech,
chunks.st: but neither vow to donate the assessment of a person nor take a vow of valuation,

chunks.en: because they do not have enough understanding.
chunks.st: because they lack the presumed mental competence to make a commitment.

chunks.en: A baby less than one month old
chunks.st: A child less than one month old is

chunks.en: can have his worth vowed, but cannot be given an erech.
chunks.explain: The Torah gives no erech for a baby younger than a month.
chunks.st: the object of a vow if others vowed to donate his assessment, but is not valuated
chunks.stMore: if one vowed to donate his fixed value, as the Torah did not establish a value for anyone less than a month old.

summary: Can a non-Jew promise an erech, or be given one? Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda argue.

chunks.en: A non-Jew: Rabbi Meir says he can be given an erech,
chunks.st: With regard to a gentile, Rabbi Meir says: He is valuated
chunks.stMore: in a case where a Jew says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the fixed value of this gentile.

words.note: A great Tanna of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: but he cannot promise an erech.
chunks.st: But a gentile does not take a vow of valuation
chunks.stMore: to donate his fixed value or the value of others.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

words.note: A great Tanna of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he can promise an erech, but he cannot be given an erech.
chunks.st: He takes a vow of valuation, but is not valuated.

chunks.en: Both of them agree
chunks.st: And both this tanna, Rabbi Meir, and that tanna, Rabbi Yehuda, agree that

chunks.en: that a non-Jew can vow a worth and can have his worth vowed.
chunks.st: gentiles vow to donate the assessment of another and are the object of vows, whereby one donates the assessment of a gentile.

summary: Someone who is about to die cannot have his worth vowed. The Tannaim argue whether he can be given an erech.

chunks.en: Someone who is about to die, and someone being taken out to be punished with death by the court,
chunks.st: One who is moribund and one who is taken to be executed after being sentenced by the court

chunks.en: cannot have his worth vowed or be given an erech.
chunks.explain: He has no worth, because no one would buy him.
chunks.st: is neither the object of a vow nor valuated.

chunks.en: Rabbi Chanina ben Akavya says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Akavya says:
chunks.stMore: He is not the object of a vow, because he has no market value;

chunks.en: he can be given an erech, because his erech is set by the Torah,
chunks.st: but he is valuated, due to the fact that one’s value is fixed

chunks.he: אֲבָל אֵינוֹ נִדָּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁאֵין דָּמָיו קְצוּבִין.
chunks.en: but his worth cannot be vowed, because his worth is not set.
chunks.st: by the Torah based on age and sex.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

words.note: A great Tanna of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: he can vow a worth, promise an erech, and make things hekdesh.
chunks.explain: Hekdesh means it now belongs to the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: One with that status vows to donate the assessment of another person to the Temple treasury, and takes vows of valuation, and consecrates his property;

chunks.en: And if he damages something,
chunks.st: and if he damages the property of others,

chunks.en: he must pay for it.
chunks.st: he is liable to pay compensation.

summary: When the court must punish a woman with death and she is expecting a baby, does the court wait? And may we use anything from her or from an animal that was put to death?

chunks.en: A woman who is being taken out to be punished with death by the court,
chunks.st: In the case of a pregnant woman who is taken by the court to be executed,

chunks.en: we do not wait for her until she has her baby.
chunks.st: the court does not wait to execute her until she gives birth.

chunks.en: If she already sat on the birthing chair,
chunks.st: But with regard to a woman taken to be executed who sat on the travailing chair [hamashber] in the throes of labor,

chunks.en: we wait for her until she has her baby.
chunks.st: the court waits to execute her until she gives birth.

chunks.en: A woman who was put to death by the court,
chunks.st: In the case of a woman who was killed through court-imposed capital punishment,

chunks.en: we may use her hair.
chunks.st: one may derive benefit from her hair.

chunks.en: An animal that was put to death by the court,
chunks.st: But in the case of an animal that was killed through court-imposed execution, e.g., for goring a person,

chunks.en: we may not use it or benefit from it at all.
chunks.st: deriving benefit from the animal is prohibited.
